feedback:
Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Unapproved external/generated IRI(s): http://qudt.org/schema/qudt, http://qudt.org/schema/qudtnumericValue, http://qudt.org/schema/qudtunit
Semantic validator feedback: Correct the QUDT prefix and all expanded QUDT paths: the current prefix produces unapproved IRIs http://qudt.org/schema/qudtnumericValue and http://qudt.org/schema/qudtunit; use the canonical QUDT namespace with the required separator. Add a constraint for requiredHullStructuralSteelGrade on each steelGradeRequirementCase enforcing exactly one value when the table selection is applicable and zero values for NOT_APPLICABLE selections. The current SPARQL NA branch incorrectly passes when any required grade exists, and the applicable branch can pass with duplicate required grades because it only tests for one matching value. Ensure the table lookup logic and applicability boundary match tableModel exactly, including explicit non-applicable rows, rather than treating unsupported thickness or selector combinations as an arbitrary NA result.

Reject. Preserve the prior cardinality repair: requiredHullStructuralSteelGrade must be exactly one for every applicable table selection and zero for every NOT_APPLICABLE selection; the current applicable SPARQL only tests that one matching value exists, so duplicate required grades pass, and the property shape lacks conditional minCount. Replace the lookup logic with the exact tableModel: the current IF mapping is wrong for multiple steelMaterialClassThree cases, including high-tensile PC6-7 at thickness 25–35 mm and high-tensile PC1-3 at thickness above 35 mm, and normal-strength class-three PC6-7 at 25–35 mm. Also make the rank comparison family-scoped to the case steelStrengthCategory; the current query compares ranks without ensuring actual and required grades belong to the same strength family, allowing cross-family grades with equal or higher numeric ranks to pass. Keep the corrected QUDT namespace and preserve the explicit NOT_APPLICABLE boundary.

Reject. Preserve the prior QUDT namespace, conditional requiredHullStructuralSteelGrade cardinality, exact tableModel, and family-scoped rank instructions. The first SPARQL FILTER has inverted pass logic: it selects valid applicable cases (matching required grade with no mismatch) and valid NOT_APPLICABLE cases (no required grade) as violations, so invalid data can pass. Rewrite it to report violations only: unsupported thickness or missing selectors must fail; applicable selections require exactly one required grade equal to the table result; NOT_APPLICABLE selections require zero required grades. Replace the IF lookup with the exact tableModel: in particular, high-tensile steelMaterialClassThree PC6-7 requires DH through 35 mm and EH above 35 mm, and PC4-5 requires EH through 45 mm and FH above 45 mm; normal class-three PC1-3 and PC4-5 selections above their declared boundaries must be NOT_APPLICABLE rather than the case node or an arbitrary grade. Ensure the query's parent is typed nltl:ship, keep the rank comparison restricted to the case steelStrengthCategory, and add a steelGradeValue constraint for steelGradeOrderRank with xsd:integer, exactly one value, so the comparison operand is declared and validated.

Preserve the prior QUDT namespace, exact conditional requiredHullStructuralSteelGrade cardinality, family-scoped rank comparison, typed ship parent, and steelGradeOrderRank xsd:integer shape. The SPARQL still does not implement tableModel exactly: for steelMaterialClassThree and thickness >35 to <=45 mm, normal-strength PC1-3 is NOT_APPLICABLE while PC4-5 and PC6-7 require E; high-tensile PC1-3 requires FH while PC4-5 and PC6-7 require EH, not FH for all Polar Classes. For thickness >45 to <=50 mm, normal-strength PC1-3 and PC4-5 are NOT_APPLICABLE and PC6-7 requires E; high-tensile PC1-3 and PC4-5 require FH while PC6-7 requires EH. Restrict the NOT_APPLICABLE PC4-5 branch to thickness >45, add the missing applicable high-tensile PC1-3/PC4-5 branches at >45, and split the >35-to-45 high-tensile branch by Polar Class. Ensure every applicable row requires exactly one matching grade, every explicit NOT_APPLICABLE row requires zero grades, and unsupported selector or thickness combinations fail rather than passing through an overbroad NA branch.
